newsitem.title: USA: World Satellite to merge with firm.
newsitem.headline: World Satellite to merge with firm.

text.p: World Satellite Network Inc said Monday it entered into a letter of intent to merge privately owned Heifner Communications Inc with WSN.
World Satellite is the largest distributor of satellite television programming to the private cable and wireless television industry and Heifner is the second largest.

Separately, World Satellite Network said Christopher Tyson of Austin, Texas, and Robert Vogelsang of Rosenburg, Texas, took undisclosed stakes in the company. The size of their investments were not disclosed.
Tyson also was named president of World Satellite, replacing Gary Hokkanen, former chief executive officer and president, who resigned in October 1996 for health reasons.
Vogelsang was named vice chairman of the company.

Commenting on the merger with Heifner, Bob Ringstad, chief operating officer said, "Until now, WSN has been unable to offer technical services in addition to cable television programming. The combination of WSN and HCI will enable us to provide those services to our installed customer base."
For the fiscal year ended August 31, 1996, WSN reported revenues of $26.2 million. Heifner generated approximately $5.6 million in calendar 1996.
Greg Heifner, who founded Heifner Communications, will remain president of that operation and is expected to join the World Satellite board after the transaction is completed.

World Satellite also said it entered into a letter of intent to merge Vogelsang's publishing and trade show businesses, National Satellite Publishing Inc and Globex Exposition Holdings LC, into it. Terms were not disclosed and the deal is pending a definitive agreement.
